newsitem.title: INDIA: India opposes foreign stake in Indian Airlines.
newsitem.headline: India opposes foreign stake in Indian Airlines.

text.p: Indian Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim was quoted on Tuesday as saying the government will not allow a foreign stake in state-run Indian Airlines.

"Indian Airlines is a symbol of the country's pride and prestige and the government will not allow any foreign investment in Indian Airlines," the Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency quoted him as telling parliament.
India allowed private airlines to fly on domestic air routes under an economic liberalisation programme that began in 1991. However, Indian Airlines continues to dominate domestic market share.
